page: Microsoft Azure D128ads_v7 is a high-capacity general-purpose server belonging to the Dadsv7 family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor using the x86_64 architecture, offering 128 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 64 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz and features advanced instruction sets including AVX-512, AVX_VNNI, and cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA_NI. The system is equipped with 512 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4 GB of RAM per vCPU.

This instance features a substantial 7559 GB local NVMe SSD, making it highly capable of handling data-intensive operations locally. In benchmark evaluations, the D128ads_v7 demonstrates top-tier performance across both single-core and multi-core workloads, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 233122.22 and a PassMark CPU score of 133871.81. Memory bandwidth is exceptionally high, reaching 12266.71 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 389.75 GB/sec for large-block reads.

Given its hardware profile, the server is highly cost-efficient for workloads requiring dense local storage and massive parallel processing without the overhead of dedicated GPU hardware. Benchmark data highlights its efficiency in database operations, achieving 177.38 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and top-tier performance in static web serving at 107.2 GB/sec. It is also highly capable for CPU-based large language model inference, processing medium 7B models at 330.81 tokens per second. This makes the instance ideal for large-scale relational databases, high-throughput web serving, and intensive ETL data pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure D128ads_v7 is a high-performance general-purpose server from the Dadsv7 family, powered by a 128-vCPU AMD EPYC 9V45 processor operating at 4.5 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture with 64 physical cores, it features 512 GB of RAM and a massive 7559 GB local NVMe SSD. The server delivers top-tier performance in multi-core processing, memory bandwidth, and database operations, as evidenced by its Redis SET throughput of 177.38 million operations per second and a PassMark CPU score of 133871.81. Lacking a dedicated GPU, it relies on advanced CPU instructions like AVX-512 for vector calculations. This configuration is highly efficient for large-scale databases, high-throughput web serving, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
